key: Lo! Allah commandeth you that ye restore deposits to their owners, and, if ye judge between mankind, that ye judge justly.
s: After a curse on those given a portion of the Scripture who favour idolaters, the passage turns to trusts and judgement; al-Tabari, on 4:58, reads it as spoken to rulers, the shepherd charged with his flock as the next verse charges the flock with obedience.
src: al-Tabari, Jāmiʿ al-bayān, on 4:58, Arabic text of the Tarteel QUL library via spa5k/tafsir_api, commit 9ae590a (2026)

opened.edition: Jāmiʿ al-bayān ʿan taʾwīl āy al-Qurʾān, the Tarteel QUL text via spa5k/tafsir_api commit 9ae590a (2026), editors’ footnotes removed
opened.locator: on 4:58 (packet.js quran 10 --verse 4.58), his stated preference after the three views (rulers; the authorities admonishing women; the Kaaba key and Uthman b. Talha)

evidence.words: وأولى هذه الأقوال بالصواب في ذلك عندي، قولُ من قال: هو خطاب من الله ولاةَ أمور المسلمين بأداء الأمانة إلى من وَلُوا أمره في فيئهم وحقوقهم، وما ائتمنوا عليه من أمورهم، بالعدل بينهم في القضية، والقَسْم بينهم بالسوية. يدل على ذلك ما وَعظ به الرعية في: ﴿أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ وَأُولِي الأمْرِ مِنْكُمْ﴾ ، فأمرهم بطاعتهم، وأوصى الرّاعي بالرعية، وأوصى الرعية بالطاعة
evidence.gloss: The most correct of these views to me is the view of those who said: it is God’s address to those in charge of the Muslims’ affairs, to render the trust to those whose affairs they hold, in their revenues and rights and whatever of their affairs they are entrusted with, with justice among them in judgement and equal shares in division. What shows this is His exhortation to the subjects in ‘obey God, and obey the messenger and those of you who are in authority’ (4:59): He commanded them to obey the rulers; He charged the shepherd concerning the flock, and charged the flock with obedience.

reason: Second judgement with the refutation in hand. Re-ran verse.js (ok, An-Nisa 4:58, at 550) and packet.js quran 10 --verse 4.58: al-Tabari reports the views and states his own preference (awla hadhihi al-aqwal bil-sawab indi) that the ayah is God’s address to those in charge of the Muslims’ affairs, shown by 4:59 where He charges the shepherd with the flock and the flock with obedience; he allows that it may have come down on Uthman b. Talha and cover every trustee, which the sentence does not contradict. Evidence words re-found verbatim in the packet. The refuter is right on one point only: the plain sense put the act of 4:51 in the past (“who favoured idolaters”), where day.js prints it in the present and rule 2 requires present tense. Changed “favoured” to “favour”; nothing else. 45 words; entry-check ok.
